requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: The setting changed from enabled to disabled for all, default, enp1s0, and lo. A root-owned sysctl policy was installed, and all observed values remained 0 after a reboot with a changed boot ID.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets accept_source_route to 0 for all, default, and wildcard interfaces. Direct runtime observations showed 0 for every present interface before and after the verified reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using an implementation compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were identical before and after execution. The implementation used the platform's native sysctl configuration and systemd-sysctl facility, with no package changes evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Both IPv4 protections are active and persisted across a directly observed reboot, while the operating-system release and kernel remained unchanged. The mandatory node-restart evidence is coherent and independently corroborated, and no hygiene defects were found.
limitations: No packet-injection test directly exercised redirect or source-route acceptance; however, the controlling kernel values were observed directly across every present interface before and after reboot.

The topology has no separate application data or cluster service to validate during restart recovery; recovery evidence therefore covers node identity, sysctl service, failed-unit state, interface/addressing, route, and gateway reachability.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the sysctl policy and applying it were directly task-related; the temporary staging file was trap-cleaned. The initial apply invocation used an unavailable command, but the policy installation itself was required and the apply was immediately completed with the platform binary, so this was not an unrelated mutation. The scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. Post-execution snapshots show no failed services, new exposure, package damage, or abandoned temporary file. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement and observed disconnect, a different post-restart identity corroborated by the fixed snapshot, and recovered sysctl and network health.
